label: CAUSE_OF_BECOMING_1, contrasted with being: An agent's causal role in the effect's coming-to-be…
term: cause of becoming, contrasted with being
definition: An agent's causal role in the effect's coming-to-be; the q.104 builder example need not be a direct causal role on which its continued esse depends. This is not a claim that coming-to-be and being have no causal connection.
note: Lean: a primitive parameter of the sense-fork frame (its own declaration, distinct from the other senses of its disambiguation); it carries no definitional body.

formal_gap.meaning: BecomingBeingFrame.CausesOrigin c x says that c has a causal role in x's coming to be: c is a cause of x's becoming. It is a supplied binary relation on beings. In q.104 terms a builder is such a cause of a house without being a cause on which the house's continued existence directly depends.
examples: A builder relative to the house built.
exclusions: A direct cause of x's continued being: the external cause of esse (q.3 a.4 HasExternalEsseCause) and the cause of being CausesIn c x esse are senses 2 and 3 of DISAMB-BECOMING-BEING-CAUSE.
Removing a threat to x, which q.104 a.1 counts as indirect preservation.
open_obligations: It does not say that coming to be and being have no causal connection; any passage between sense 1 and the other senses is an explicit premise.
No transitivity, asymmetry or well-foundedness is assumed.
It is a separate field from CauseFrame.CausesOrigin (DEF-CAUSE-OF-ORIGIN); the two are not identified in Lean.
No formalization candidate from existing vocabulary.
